questions.q: How long before he needs to has Stephen Kumalo arrived at the station at Carisbrooke?
questions.explain: 'Though Stephen Kumalo has been there a full hour before he need, he does not listen to these things.' His mind is on money and worry.

questions.q: What preoccupies Kumalo's thoughts as he waits for the train?
choices: The sermon he must preach on his return
The cost of the journey and how sick his sister may be
Whether the chief will be angry
questions.explain: 'This is a long way to go, and a lot of money to pay. And who knows how sick his sister may be, and what money that may cost?'

questions.q: How does the chapter describe catching a bus in Johannesburg, compared with home?
choices: Buses run exactly on time there
There is a multitude of buses and only about one in ten or twenty is the right one
There are no buses at all
The buses are free for parsons
questions.explain: At home 'the only bus that comes is the right bus'; in Johannesburg 'only one bus in ten, one bus in twenty maybe, is the right bus.'

questions.q: Whose son was killed crossing a street in Johannesburg, a memory that feeds Kumalo's fear?
questions.explain: Mpanza's wife 'saw her son Michael killed in the street'; the twelve-year-old stepped out and 'the great lorry crushed the life out of her son.'

questions.q: What favour does Kumalo's companion at the station ask of him?
choices: To carry a letter to the Bishop
To inquire about Sibeko's daughter, who has not been heard from in Johannesburg
To buy tools for the carpenter's shop
questions.explain: Sibeko has had no word of his daughter for ten or twelve months and asks Kumalo to inquire.

questions.q: For whom had Sibeko's daughter been working before she left the district?
choices: The white man uSmith in Ixopo
questions.explain: She worked for uSmith in Ixopo, then went with uSmith's married daughter to Johannesburg to work.

questions.q: To what place near Johannesburg does the paper say Sibeko's daughter went?
questions.explain: Kumalo reads the thumbed paper: 'Springs... I have heard of the place. But it is not Johannesburg, though they say it is near.'

questions.q: Which carriage does Kumalo climb into on the train?
choices: The carriage for non-Europeans, full of the humbler people of his race
questions.explain: He climbs 'into the carriage for non-Europeans, already full of the humbler people of his race.'

questions.q: What 'little vanity' or 'little lie' does Kumalo tell the other passengers?
choices: That he goes often to Johannesburg and has many things to do there
That his son is a lawyer
That he owns land on the tops
questions.explain: He tells them, 'when I am in Johannesburg I shall go to this place at Springs... I have many things to do in Johannesburg' — then feels his knees go weak, having 'told his little lie, before these respectful people.'

questions.q: What does the 'humble man' take out of his pocket as the journey begins and the fear returns?
choices: His sacred book, and begins to read
questions.explain: 'The humble man reached in his pocket for his sacred book, and began to read. It was this world alone that was certain.'
